features.name: a cleanup step names its root cause
features.description: A step that deletes or restarts things to clear a symptom must point to its root cause (feat, issue or PROGRESS entry). Found 2026-10-23: 'delete dead pods' hid hangar's graceful-shutdown bug.
acceptance_criteria: a cleanup step without a cause reference is flagged
features.evidence: templates/hooks/common/handover-guard.sh: in scripts/handover/*.sh a cleanup step (kubectl delete, rollout restart, rm -r in any flag order, docker rm; continued lines joined, last line included) needs '# cause: <feat-NNN|ABC-123|#12|URL|PROGRESS>' directly above or trailing; the error names the line. Owner choice 2026-10-25: extend handover-guard. scripts/tests/test_handover_guard.sh 83/83 (bash 3.2); hangar's script passes; 11 gates OK. Two review rounds (2 subagents each; round 2's security result arrived after its fixes and led to a third fix pass) found flag orders, quoted trailing causes, $( ), 'because:', continuation, a quadratic comment strip (128 s on 160 KB, now ~1 s) and name=value paths, all fixed test-first. Known limits in the guard header.

features.name: architecture.md matches the two-layer harness
features.description: architecture.md says Python 3.14.7, ~/.gemini/skills, statuses done/in-progress, and leaves out agent-harness.json, skill packs, global hooks, the runtime dir and target-repos.txt. Rewrite after feat-103 to feat-105 so it describes the final layout once.
acceptance_criteria: every path, version and status value in architecture.md exists in the repo or host as written
the two-layer harness has its own section
features.evidence: Fixed 3.14.7 to 3.14.9 (3 places), ~/.gemini/skills to the real per-agent dirs, statuses to planned/in_progress/completed, the deleted harness/guards hooks to the templates with their knobs; added section 2.5 (two-layer harness: target-repos.txt, agent-harness.json, harness_adapter check/drift/sync/sync-all, runtime dir, global hooks, packs) and layout rows for .agents, .codex, config/skill-packs.json. A script checked every backticked path: all exist in the repo or under ~, except runtime-relative names (hooks/*.sh, harness-version.json), target-repo files and generic or example names. Docs only, no review.
